title: Prometheus
description: Health of the lab's Prometheus server (prometheus-kps-0): ingestion, TSDB/WAL, cardinality, scraping, rule evaluation, OTLP ingestion and alert delivery to Alertmanager. Curated from the official prometheus-mixin (https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tree/main/documentation/prometheus-mixin) and its alert rules shipped by kube-prometheus-stack. The chart's own 'Prometheus / Overview' dashboard (folder Kubernetes) stays as the upstream reference.

list.name: Firing alerts
list.textFormat: Prometheus ALERTS series in state firing. See Alertmanager / alert rules for details.

list.name: Container restarts
list.textFormat: kube-state-metrics saw the restart counter change (crash, OOMKill or liveness failure).

list.name: Config reloads
list.textFormat: A new scrape/rule config was loaded (the config-reloader sidecar triggers it when the operator re-renders ServiceMonitors/PrometheusRules).

list.name: TSDB head compactions
list.textFormat: Head block persisted / blocks merged (normally every 2h).

options.content:
**Prometheus** stores every metric of the lab (scraped from ServiceMonitors/PodMonitors in all namespaces,
plus OTLP pushed by the otel-gateway at `/api/v1/otlp`) and evaluates all alerting/recording rules. Single replica,
retention 15 days / 18 GiB on `local-path`.

**Healthy looks like**: *Up* = UP, *Config* = OK, samples/s flat, head series stable (no staircase), 0 rule failures,
0 targets down, 0 notification errors, WAL/TSDB failure panels flat at 0.

**When something goes red**
- *Config FAILED* → a PrometheusRule or ServiceMonitor broke the config: `kubectl --context k8s01 -n monitoring logs prometheus-kps-0 -c prometheus | grep -i error`.
- *Head series climbing / churn high* → a cardinality explosion: the *Samples per scrape* and *Series churn* panels name the job; fix the exporter or drop labels with `metricRelabelings`.
- *Targets down* → see the *Targets per job* table, then `kubectl get endpoints` for that Service.
- *Rule failures / missed iterations* → the query of a rule errors or a group takes longer than its interval.
- *Notification errors* → Prometheus cannot reach Alertmanager (see the Alertmanager dashboard).

Formulas come from the [prometheus-mixin](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tree/main/documentation/prometheus-mixin) dashboards and alerts (thresholds mirror the kube-prometheus-stack
`prometheus` rule group). Storage: [docs](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/storage/).

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Scrape health of the Prometheus container itself (`up`). DOWN means Prometheus is not running or cannot scrape itself: nothing else on this page (and no alert) can be trusted.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the Prometheus process started (`process_start_time_seconds`). A small value right after an unexpected drop means a restart (OOMKill?): check the restart annotation.

panels.title: Config
panels.description: Result of the last configuration reload (`prometheus_config_last_reload_successful`). FAILED means Prometheus keeps running the previous config and ignores new targets/rules. Mixin alert PrometheusBadConfig (critical) fires when it is 0 for 10m.

panels.title: Head series
panels.description: Active series in the in-memory head block (`prometheus_tsdb_head_series`), i.e. the current cardinality. Memory use grows roughly linearly with it. Watch the trend, not the absolute value.

panels.title: Samples / s
panels.description: Ingestion rate: samples appended to the head per second (scrapes + OTLP + rule results). Formula from the mixin 'Appended Samples' panel. A drop to 0 means Prometheus stopped ingesting (alert PrometheusNotIngestingSamples).

panels.title: Targets down
panels.description: Number of scrape targets whose last scrape failed (`up == 0`) across the whole cluster. kube-prometheus alert TargetDown fires when >10% of a job's targets are down for 10m. Details in the 'Targets per job' table.

panels.title: Rule failures (1h)
panels.description: Rule evaluations that returned an error in the last hour (`prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total`). Any failure means an alert or recording rule is silently not working. Mixin alert PrometheusRuleFailures (critical) fires on any increase.

panels.title: Alert send errors (1h)
panels.description: Errors sending alerts to Alertmanager in the last hour (`prometheus_notifications_errors_total`). Mixin alerts PrometheusErrorSendingAlertsTo(Some|Any)Alertmanager(s) fire above 1% of sends.

panels.title: Disk used / limit
panels.description: On-disk size (persisted blocks + WAL + memory-mapped head chunks) as a share of the size-based retention limit (`prometheus_tsdb_retention_limit_bytes`, 18 GiB). Near 100% Prometheus deletes the oldest blocks early (size retention), so you get less than 15 days of history. Metric semantics: Prometheus storage docs.

panels.title: Samples appended / s
panels.description: Samples written to the TSDB head per second, by sample type (float / native histogram). Source: mixin 'Appended Samples' (`rate(prometheus_tsdb_head_samples_appended_total[5m])`). A sudden jump means a new target or a label explosion; a drop to 0 means ingestion stopped.

panels.title: Head series and chunks
panels.description: Active series (`prometheus_tsdb_head_series`, mixin 'Head Series') and how fast series are created/removed (right axis would hide it, so it is per minute). Steady creation with no matching removal = growing cardinality; spikes every 2h are normal head GC after compaction.

panels.title: Out-of-order / too old samples
panels.description: Samples rejected by the TSDB because they are older than the head accepts (`prometheus_tsdb_out_of_order_samples_total`, `prometheus_tsdb_too_old_samples_total`, `prometheus_tsdb_out_of_bound_samples_total`). Usually OTLP pushes with delayed timestamps or duplicated exporters. Should be 0; the mixin alerts PrometheusOutOfOrderTimestamps / DuplicateTimestamps cover the scrape side.

panels.title: Samples per scrape - top 10 jobs
panels.description: Samples kept per scrape after relabeling (`scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling`, an automatically generated series documented in https://prometheus.io/docs/concepts/jobs_instances/), summed per job. This is the per-job cardinality: the biggest bars are where to cut labels/metrics when head series grow.

panels.title: Series churn - top 10 jobs (new series / 1h)
panels.description: New series created per job over the last hour (`sum_over_time(scrape_series_added[1h])`; `scrape_series_added` is the documented per-scrape count of new series). High churn (pod restarts, labels with IDs/timestamps) bloats the head and the index even when the current series count looks fine.

panels.title: Targets per job
panels.description: One line per scrape job: targets up, targets total, samples kept per scrape and the slowest scrape. A job with up < total has failing targets (alert TargetDown). Scrape duration close to the 30s interval means the exporter is too slow and scrapes overlap/time out. Sources: `up`, `scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling`, `scrape_duration_seconds` (Prometheus docs, automatically generated series).

panels.title: Targets down by job
panels.description: Count of targets with `up == 0`, per job. Empty/flat at 0 is healthy. kube-prometheus rule TargetDown: `100 * count by (job, namespace, service) (up == 0) / count(up) > 10` for 10m.

panels.title: Slowest scrapes - top 10
panels.description: Per-target scrape duration (`scrape_duration_seconds`). Values approaching the scrape interval (30s) or timeout (10s default) lead to failed scrapes.

panels.title: Scrape errors by cause
panels.description: Samples/scrapes rejected while scraping. Body size / sample limit = target exceeded a configured limit (whole scrape dropped); duplicate / out-of-order timestamps = broken exporter. Formula: mixin 'Scrape failures' panel. Mixin alerts PrometheusScrapeSampleLimitHit, PrometheusScrapeBodySizeLimitHit, PrometheusDuplicateTimestamps, PrometheusOutOfOrderTimestamps.

panels.title: Service discovery
panels.description: Targets discovered by Kubernetes SD (mixin 'Discovered targets', `prometheus_sd_discovered_targets`) and SD failures (`prometheus_sd_kubernetes_failures_total`, alert PrometheusKubernetesListWatchFailures). Failures mean Prometheus cannot list/watch the API server and target lists go stale.

panels.title: Target sync / scrape pool reloads
panels.description: Time to sync target lists (`prometheus_target_sync_length_seconds`, mixin 'Target Sync') and failures (`prometheus_target_sync_failed_total`, alert PrometheusTargetSyncFailure (critical); `prometheus_target_scrape_pool_reloads_failed_total`).

panels.title: Average scrape interval
panels.description: Actual interval between scrapes, by configured interval (mixin 'Average Scrape Interval Duration': `rate(prometheus_target_interval_length_seconds_sum[5m]) / rate(prometheus_target_interval_length_seconds_count[5m])`). It should match the configured value (30s); drift means Prometheus is overloaded.

panels.title: Rule evaluation failures
panels.description: Failed evaluations per rule group (`prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total`). A failing rule silently stops alerting. Mixin alert PrometheusRuleFailures (critical): any increase in 5m.

panels.title: Missed iterations
panels.description: Rule group evaluations skipped because the previous one was still running (`prometheus_rule_group_iterations_missed_total`). Mixin alert PrometheusMissingRuleEvaluations.

panels.title: Slowest rule groups (duration / interval)
panels.description: Last evaluation duration divided by the group interval (`prometheus_rule_group_last_duration_seconds / prometheus_rule_group_interval_seconds`, the ratio behind the upstream rule-group 'evaluation slow' condition). Above 1 (100%) the group cannot finish in time and iterations are missed.

panels.title: Rule evaluation latency
panels.description: Per-rule evaluation duration quantiles (`prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds`, a summary) and total evaluations/s. Long evaluations usually come from heavy recording rules over many series.

panels.title: Rules and evaluations / s
panels.description: Loaded rules (`prometheus_rule_group_rules`) and evaluations per second (`prometheus_rule_evaluations_total`). A sudden drop in loaded rules after a reload means a PrometheusRule was removed or rejected by the operator (see Prometheus Operator dashboard).

panels.title: Storage size
panels.description: On-disk usage split into persisted blocks (`prometheus_tsdb_storage_blocks_bytes`), write-ahead log (`prometheus_tsdb_wal_storage_size_bytes`) and memory-mapped head chunks, with the size-retention limit (18 GiB). Data lives on the node disk (local-path).

panels.title: Compactions and reloads
panels.description: Compactions (`prometheus_tsdb_compactions_total`) and failures (`prometheus_tsdb_compactions_failed_total`, `prometheus_tsdb_reloads_failures_total`). Mixin alerts PrometheusTSDBCompactionsFailing / PrometheusTSDBReloadsFailing fire on any failure in 3h: failing compactions make the WAL and head grow until the disk fills.

panels.title: WAL failures
panels.description: Write-ahead-log problems: corruptions, failed writes, failed truncations and failed checkpoints (`prometheus_tsdb_wal_*_failed_total`, `prometheus_tsdb_wal_corruptions_total`, `prometheus_tsdb_checkpoint_creations_failed_total`, `prometheus_tsdb_head_truncations_failed_total`). All must stay at 0; anything else usually means a full or broken disk.

panels.title: WAL fsync latency
panels.description: Time to fsync the WAL to disk (`prometheus_tsdb_wal_fsync_duration_seconds`, summary). Slow fsync (tens of ms and up) means the node disk is saturated, which slows ingestion of every sample. Gaps (NaN) are normal when no fsync happened in the summary window.

panels.title: Head chunks / blocks loaded
panels.description: Chunks in the head (`prometheus_tsdb_head_chunks`, mixin 'Head Chunks') and number of persisted blocks loaded (`prometheus_tsdb_blocks_loaded`). Blocks loaded should stay roughly constant once retention is reached.

panels.title: Retention
panels.description: Data removed by time retention (`prometheus_tsdb_time_retentions_total`) vs by size retention (`prometheus_tsdb_size_retentions_total`), plus the age of the oldest sample. Size retentions mean disk pressure cuts history below the 15-day target.

panels.title: OTLP write requests by status
panels.description: Requests to the OTLP receiver (`prometheus_http_requests_total{handler="/api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics"}`), by HTTP code, plus the remote-write receiver. The otel-gateway pushes span metrics, service-graph metrics and app metrics here. Non-2xx codes = rejected batches (look at the gateway's exporter failures on the OpenTelemetry Collectors dashboard). Flat at 0 while no app sends telemetry.

panels.title: OTLP request latency
panels.description: Latency of OTLP write requests (`prometheus_http_request_duration_seconds` histogram, handler /api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics). Empty until the first OTLP request arrives (the histogram is created lazily).

panels.title: OTLP data quality
panels.description: Samples appended through OTLP without metric metadata (`prometheus_api_otlp_appended_samples_without_metadata_total`) and OTLP exemplars rejected as out of order (`prometheus_api_otlp_out_of_order_exemplars_total`). Not errors that drop samples, but signs of malformed or delayed OTLP input.

panels.title: Notifications sent / errors / dropped
panels.description: Alerts sent to Alertmanager (`prometheus_notifications_sent_total`), errors (`..._errors_total`) and alerts dropped (`..._dropped_total`, e.g. queue full or relabeled away). Mixin alerts PrometheusErrorSendingAlertsToSomeAlertmanagers (>1% errors) and PrometheusErrorSendingAlertsToAnyAlertmanager (critical).

panels.title: Notification queue
panels.description: Pending alerts in the send queue (`prometheus_notifications_queue_length`) against its capacity, and Alertmanagers discovered. Mixin alerts: PrometheusNotificationQueueRunningFull (queue predicted to reach capacity in 30m) and PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers (< 1 discovered).

panels.title: Notification latency
panels.description: Time to deliver a batch of alerts to Alertmanager (`prometheus_notifications_latency_seconds`, summary). Seconds or more means Alertmanager is slow or unreachable.

panels.title: Query concurrency
panels.description: Queries running now (`prometheus_engine_queries`) vs the concurrency limit (`prometheus_engine_queries_concurrent_max`). Mixin alert PrometheusHighQueryLoad fires above 80% for 15m: dashboards and rules start queueing.

panels.title: Query latency by stage (p90)
panels.description: 90th percentile of query duration by stage (mixin 'Query Stage Duration': `max by (slice) (prometheus_engine_query_duration_seconds{quantile="0.9"})`). inner_eval dominates for heavy queries; queue_time > 0 means queries waited for a free slot.

panels.title: HTTP API errors
panels.description: API responses with 5xx codes by handler (`prometheus_http_requests_total`). Grafana panels show errors when this is non-zero; 4xx (bad queries) are excluded on purpose.

panels.title: CPU (cores)
panels.description: CPU used by the container (cAdvisor `container_cpu_usage_seconds_total`, rate) against its request (kube-state-metrics). No CPU limit is set in this lab (requests only), so the container can burst; sustained use far above the request means the request should be raised so the scheduler accounts for it. Formula: kubernetes-mixin 'Compute Resources / Pod' dashboard.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Working set (what the kernel OOM-killer looks at) against the memory request and limit. The working set reaching the limit means an OOMKill (watch the restart annotation). Formula: kubernetes-mixin 'Compute Resources / Pod' dashboard (container_memory_working_set_bytes).

panels.title: Config-reloader sidecar
panels.description: The config-reloader sidecar watches the rendered config/rules and triggers Prometheus reloads. `reloader_last_reload_successful` = 0 fires ConfigReloaderSidecarErrors (kube-prometheus-stack rule group config-reloaders).
